rationale: The child supplies only a title indicating revocation of an earlier executive order and a signature block. C04, C05, and C19 are the closest candidates because they also revoke earlier orders, but revocation is a routine governmental function and drafting form. The supplied material reveals no distinctive shared language, parallel substantive provisions, or adapted administrative machinery sufficient to show that any candidate materially templated the child.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: Paragraph 2 (b) of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of January 23, 1950 ... be, and it is hereby, revoked.
shared_material.explanation: C04 uses a concrete revocation clause, but the overlap is only the generic act of revoking an earlier directive.
C05 has the same broad revocation-document form, without disclosed distinctive language or matching machinery.
C19 similarly revokes a named prior order, but that title-level resemblance is routine and insufficient.
